sections.html: Casa Grande is a Pinal County city roughly halfway between Phoenix and Tucson, using the ZIP codes 85122, 85130, 85193 and 85194. Headcount reached an estimated 69,753 on July 1, 2025, a 29.9% increase over the 53,705 counted in April 2020. Most working residents commute toward the Phoenix area or toward Tucson, with a mean trip of 23.3 minutes. New jobs bring new renters and first-time buyers and also bring new construction, so an older house will be compared with recently built homes nearby.

Owners live in most Casa Grande homes, and the median value runs near $304,000 for 2020 to 2024. A monthly owner cost of $1,635 with a mortgage sits beside median gross rent of $1,386, a gap buyers weigh when deciding whether to buy.

The City of Casa Grande Building Division issues permits for construction, alteration, repair, installation, demolition and occupancy-related work. The city lists additions, remodeling, structural work, pools and spas, solar systems, accessory structures and mechanical, electrical, plumbing or gas work as common permit projects, and the Building Division makes the final call. If you're unsure, contact the Development Center before starting. The Building Division is at 510 E. Florence Blvd and answers at 520-421-8630.

If a previous owner added a room, a patio cover or a pool, ask the Building Division for the permit record before you list or accept an offer. Finished work should have a passed final inspection, and a building should not be occupied until any required certificate of occupancy is issued. Heat is hard on roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes, and a buyer's inspector is likely to check them, so know their age.

A landlord who rented a house short term and now wants to sell should know the city's ordinance, No. 1397.05.06, which took effect January 1, 2025. Because A.R.S. 9-500.39 permits short-term rentals in every Arizona city, Casa Grande uses a permit rather than a ban. An owner's steps are:

  • Obtain a Transaction Privilege Tax license through the Arizona Department of Revenue.
  • Notify the Pinal County Assessor's Office of the rental status.
  • Apply for the city permit, which costs $115 and renews annually for $115.
  • Notify neighbors next door and across the street, and file the attestation within seven business days of getting the permit.
  • Post the owner and emergency contact where guests can see it.

Operating without a permit can bring civil penalties of up to $1,000 for every 30 days after a 30-day notice. Rules and fees change, so read the city's short-term rental page before relying on these figures.

sections.h2: Deed, recording and property tax in a Casa Grande sale
sections.html:
Recording a Casa Grande sale happens at the Pinal County Recorder, for a standard $30 per document. The fee schedule, effective July 1, 2019, folds in the affidavit of property value, extra indexing and a $1 charge for mailing the document back.

Each deed must come with an affidavit of legal value under A.R.S. 11-1133, signed by buyer and seller or their agents. The form lists the sale price, the date, the parcel number and whether the buyer will live in the home or rent it. A deed with an incomplete affidavit gets refused, unless it notes an A.R.S. 11-1134 exemption such as a deed of gift or a court-ordered conveyance. Title and escrow companies usually prepare all of this for you.

Pinal County parcels with bills over $100 are paid in two halves. October 1 is the first due date, with delinquency after 5 p.m. on November 1. March 1 is the second, with delinquency after 5 p.m. on May 1. A weekend or holiday pushes delinquency to the next business day. Late balances accrue 16% a year, prorated monthly.

Ask the Pinal County Treasurer for a payoff that includes any prior-year taxes and interest, and give the number to the title company before the contract is signed. An owner who lets a tax installment slide still has to clear it at closing, so the cash you receive is the price minus that balance and any loan payoff.

A cash sale doesn't change that math. It only removes the lender's appraisal and underwriting from the timeline, because the buyer isn't borrowing. What stays is the same short list: a settled tax balance, a clean deed, a complete affidavit or exemption notation, and a recorded transfer. If any of those is open on the day you accept an offer, tell the buyer and the title company right away, and ask the Pinal County Treasurer or the Recorder what it will take to close it out. Doing that before the contract is signed keeps the closing date from slipping.

sections.h2: How a Casa Grande closing goes
sections.html: After you accept an offer, the title or escrow company opens a file, requests payoff figures, and drafts the deed and affidavit. You sign the deed, and the company records it with the Pinal County Recorder and pays you from the proceeds. Before you reach that stage, line up the permit record for any addition, pool or solar work, and if you rented short term, close out the city permit and the state license. Tell the Pinal County Assessor's Office when the rental status changes.

sections.h2: Paperwork to collect before you list
sections.html:
Cash buyers move quickly, so have these items ready.

  • The deed and parcel number, which identify the property on every form.
  • The Pinal County tax bill, with a note of which half is paid.
  • Permit records and final inspection results for any addition, pool, solar system or accessory structure.
  • If the house was a short-term rental, the city permit, the Transaction Privilege Tax license and proof the Assessor's Office was notified.
  • A loan payoff figure, if a mortgage remains.

A permit record has to be looked up by the Building Division, so call 520-421-8630 early and let the rest of the list wait. For a pool or an addition, ask for the final inspection result at the same time, because the record is only useful with it. Keep copies of whatever they send, and hand a set to the title company so a buyer's questions can be answered the same day.

faqs.q: How many people live in Casa Grande?
faqs.a: The estimate is 69,753 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 53,705 in April 2020. The city sits in Pinal County between Phoenix and Tucson.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Casa Grande?
faqs.a: The Pinal County Recorder charges $30 for most documents, including a deed, and the fee covers the affidavit of property value and return postage. Your title or escrow company usually pays it at closing.

faqs.q: Does a Casa Grande rental need a city permit?
faqs.a: Yes, any property rented for less than 30 days needs a Casa Grande Short-Term Rental Permit, which costs $115 a year. Owners also need a state Transaction Privilege Tax license and must notify the Pinal County Assessor and nearby neighbors.

faqs.q: When are Pinal County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes over $100 are due in halves, October 1 and March 1, and become delinquent after 5 p.m. on the following November 1 and May 1. Late payments accrue 16% simple interest per year, prorated monthly.

faqs.q: Who do I call about permits for work done on my Casa Grande house?
faqs.a: The Building Division, at 510 E. Florence Blvd or 520-421-8630. Ask for the permit record on any addition, pool or solar system before you list.
